old: It began as a word for wide, open ground, long before it meant marching orders or ballot boxes.
Its ancestor meant a military operation carried out across open country.
It shares its root with champagne — both trace back to a flat, open field.
clues: This noun for a kind of organized undertaking traces back to a simple Latin word meaning a plain, open field.
It names a sustained, planned series of actions toward one goal, like winning votes or selling a product, not a one-off push. Armies once used it for battlefield operations.
Candidates hit the trail for one before election day, and it shares its ancient field root with champagne, the sparkling wine.
